confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on two web searches. One returned aggregated cost-of-living figures from CityCost, NomadRanker, Nomad Watch, Livingcost and Expat Exchange. Those figures were roughly USD 3-3.50 for a cheap meal, USD 1.30-1.50 for a domestic draft beer, USD 2-2.65 for a cappuccino and about USD 19.60 for a mid-range dinner for two. I raised them moderately because tourist-area cafes and restaurants in General Luna usually charge more than crowdsourced island-wide averages. I also widened the mid-range meal estimate because one source's USD 4 figure for two people is implausible. I did not search for cocktail or wine prices. Cocktails are estimated at about 3-3.5 times the beer price and wine at about 3 times, which fits Philippine beach-resort patterns, so both are uncertain. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge only, not checked against current listings. They allow for July being a moderately busy, non-peak period on the island. The FX rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18 comes from a search result summary that names the RBA as its source. I did not open the RBA page itself, and a later observation may have been published since.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Siargao (General Luna) with other Philippine surf and beach tourist hubs such as El Nido and Boracay, and with Southeast Asian surf towns. Prices there sit above Philippine city averages like Cebu because of tourist demand and the cost of shipping goods to the island.
